pronunciation.approximation: Say "poliahu" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Poliahu".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "poliahu" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Poliahu" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Poliahu
domains.subtitle: Snow
domains.lead: Poliahu is snow, mauna kea. The name means "Cloaked bosom" and belongs to the polynesian tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Poliahu returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in polynesian myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Poliahu, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Poliahu place snow, mauna kea at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Poliahu appears in polynesian tradition as snow, mauna kea. The name's meaning, "Cloaked bosom", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Poliahu in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Poliahu remains a touchstone for understanding polynesian religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Craig, Robert D., Dictionary of Polynesian Mythology (1989).
